subject: BrightBridge — sudden degradations: batch alignment & KV cache churn investigation
messages:
From: John Lee <john.lee@brightbridge.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@brightbridge.ai>, BrightBridge Support <support@brightbridge.ai>
Date: 2029-01-09T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Sudden p99 spikes and errors since 08:30 PT

Evelyn —

We started seeing a big regression around 08:30 PT this morning: p99 generation latency jumped from ~480ms to 3.2s and error rate for our priority lane climbed to 4.8%. Throughput fell off as well (approx -35%). This is impacting our customer demo traffic and a handful of live sessions.

We've attached logs and a light trace bundle. Quick summary from our side:
- Errors are mostly 5xx timeouts and model failing to allocate KV pages quickly
- The errors and latency correlate with a higher-than-usual number of requests that include long prefix contexts (~6k tokens)
- No config change from our side during that window

Can you confirm this is on Redwood's side? We need immediate mitigation (fallback or throttling) while you investigate.

Thanks,
John
John Lee
Head of Platform Ops — BrightBridge AI

Attachments: support_logs_20290109.tar.gz (log bundle, ~32MB)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: John Lee <john.lee@brightbridge.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-01-09T09:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes and errors since 08:30 PT

John — thanks for the quick heads-up and the logs. We’re triaging now. Preliminary notes from the on-call runbook:
- I'll open an ops incident and loop in eng for KV cache signals.
- Karthik: can you look for HOL (head-of-line) indications on priority lanes and any sudden increase in batch sizes or blocked batches?
- Marissa: please prepare a short customer-facing note describing immediate mitigation options (fallback model, reduced max tokens).

We’ll share a short mitigation plan within 30 minutes. Apologies for the disruption — we’ll treat as P1.

– Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-01-09T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes and errors since 08:30 PT

Root-cause notes from initial triage:
- Observed repeated KV cache churn on the tenant set for BrightBridge between 08:27–08:42.
- Prefetch and prefix-cache hit rates dropped sharply; simultaneous increase in full-prefix loads which pushed batches to stall while waiting for KV loads.
- HOL blocking observed when a single long-prefix request (6k tokens) enters a shared batch lane causing subsequent short requests to wait for KV priming.
- Autoscaler and batch lane metrics show transient lane saturation — not a full node OOM, but starvation in priority lane slots.

Immediate actions taken (09:40):
- Disabled cross-tenant shared batching for BrightBridge to isolate lane behavior.
- Temporarily reduced max-batch-wait to shorten stall window.
- Eng running a KV layer debug trace (kv-config-diff-epoch-20290109.txt attached).

Next steps:
- If short-term isolation reduces p99, we will craft a targeted KV-config rollback.
- Need leadership sign-off for a temporary per-tenant cache pin (reduce eviction aggressiveness) for BB until we tune prefetch heuristics.

Karthik
Senior SRE — Redwood Inference

Attachments: kv-config-diff-epoch-20290109.txt (config snapshot diff)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Lee <john.lee@brightbridge.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-01-09T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes and errors since 08:30 PT

John — quick note for BrightBridge customers/implementers while we investigate:
- Short mitigation options you can accept now: reduce requested max_tokens by 40% for non-demo traffic, or enable our fallback model (lower-capacity variant) for demo sessions; either reduces pressure on KV priming.
- We can enable a temporary priority-lane pin for BB (requires internal approval). This prevents eviction churn but has unit-cost implications.

We’ll keep you updated every 30–60 minutes until stable. If you want us to enable fallback now, reply and we’ll flip the route.

— Marissa
Account Lead, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-01-09T11:13:00-08:00
Subject: Exec sync requested — BrightBridge P1

Evelyn / Karthik —

Customer is high-touch (enterprise demo tomorrow). Sales is asking for an exec-level note acknowledging we’ve put mitigations in place and next steps. Draft below for sign-off:

"Dear John — we understand the disruption this morning. Our engineers identified cache churn and priority-lane stalls driven by long-prefix requests and have isolated BrightBridge to prevent cross-tenant interference. We’ve enacted temporary protections (reduced batch wait, temporary cache pin) while we tune prefetch heuristics. We will continue to monitor and follow up with a post-incident summary and timeline for configuration rollback"

Please approve or edit; I can send to John within 30 minutes.

Grace
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: John Lee <john.lee@brightbridge.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-01-11T16:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: BrightBridge — post-mortem & follow-ups

John — final update and next steps. Apologies for the delay on the post-mortem. Summary:

What happened:
- A spike of long-prefix (>5k tokens) requests from BrightBridge caused repeated KV prefetches and eviction/rehydration cycles in the shared priority lane. That produced HOL blocking for short requests in the same lane, increasing p99 and error rate.

What we did (immediate):
- Isolated BB traffic from cross-tenant shared batching (temporary).
- Reduced max-batch-wait and increased small-request scheduling priority.
- Applied a temporary per-tenant cache pin (reduced eviction aggressiveness) for 24 hours.

What we will do (next 7 days):
- Roll out a prefetch heuristic update that detects long-prefix priming and routes those to a dedicated background prefetch lane (engineering ticket OPS-7876).
- Add a per-tenant eviction budget so long-prefix tenants do not push short-request latency above SLA.
- Share a detailed post-incident report and cost/impact analysis for the temporary cache pin.

Outcome: metrics returned to baseline by Jan 10 14:00 PT after mitigations; no data loss.

If you want us to revert the temporary pin earlier or keep it until the heuristic deploy, say so and we’ll coordinate.

Thank you for patience and for the clear logs — they helped a lot.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

Attachments: mitigation-runbook-draft.pdf (short-term ops playbook)
